The casing houses the impeller and diffuser, and is typically made of cast iron or steel. The impeller is a rotating component that converts the kinetic energy of the fluid into pressure. The diffuser is a stationary component that directs the fluid flow into the discharge piping.

The shaft connects the impeller to the motor, and is supported by bearings to prevent friction. The packing seal is a device used to prevent leakage of fluid between the pump and the motor. It consists of a gland, packing, and spring, and is used to create a seal that is resistant to leakage.

The motor is an electrical component that provides the power to drive the pump. It typically consists of a stator, rotor, and windings. The stator is a stationary component that generates a magnetic field. The rotor is a rotating component that is attracted to the stator, and is connected to the shaft. The windings are the conductors that carry the electrical current, and are used to create the magnetic field.
